name: opencode
one_liner: A free, open-source AI coding assistant you run yourself, similar to Claude Code, that works in your terminal or as a desktop app and lets you plug in any AI model you like.
buyer: A developer or small team that wants an AI coding assistant without being locked into one vendor's pricing or model choice, and is comfortable running open-source tools themselves.
business_use_cases: A dev tools consultancy standardizes on it for client engagements because it's free and lets them swap in whichever AI model is cheapest for a given client's budget.
A company building an internal developer platform forks it to add company-specific commands and ships it as their in-house coding assistant instead of paying per-seat for a commercial tool.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid setup and customization services (custom agents, internal tool integrations) for companies who want it wired into their existing dev stack.
Build and sell premium plugins/extensions on top of the open core, similar to how other open-source dev tools monetize.

steal_this: There isn't much of a weekend product here for an individual — this is infrastructure competing directly with well-funded incumbents. The realistic play is consulting/customization work, not a new product.
